feature.name: Model_Federation
feature.description: The root feature representing the Model Federation approach, which integrates heterogeneous models from different modeling languages and tools into a cohesive multi-model system while maintaining consistency and enabling coordinated evolution. Trace: [Article_11 §II. Background; Article_13 §3. Federating models]

feature.name: Structural
feature.description: Covers the artefacts, links, and structural features of Model Federation, including model composition, graph structure, formalism, domain, and technological context.

feature.name: Artifacts
feature.description: Represents the core entities stored and managed within the federation, including models, registries, and auxiliary data.

feature.name: Model
feature.description: A constituent model participating in the federation, conforming to a specific modeling language and representing a viewpoint or aspect of the system. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository; Article_11 §II. Background; Article_12 §II. The Role of Multimodels in MDE]

feature.name: Specification_Model
feature.description: A model that defines the system structure or behavior, such as UML class diagrams or state machines. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Model Attributes and Interfaces]

feature.name: Analytical_Model
feature.description: A model that analyzes system aspects, such as performance or reliability. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Model Attributes and Interfaces]

feature.name: Interface
feature.description: Exposes a model's inputs and outputs as attributes, defining its role in data exchange. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Model Attributes and Interfaces]

feature.name: Attributes
feature.description: Data elements exchanged between models, owned by a single model and written only by that owner. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Model Attributes and Interfaces]

feature.name: Model_Registry
feature.description: A list enumerating the models that are members of the multi-model, determining participation. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Model Registry]

feature.name: Constraints
feature.description: Rules or conditions attached to model attributes to enforce validity, triggering notifications when violated. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Constraints]

feature.name: Notifications
feature.description: Messages sent to models to inform them of events such as constraint violations or attribute changes. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Notifications]

feature.name: Federation_Model
feature.description: A model that reifies dependencies and links between federated models, serving as the central coordination artifact. Trace: [Article_11 §II. Background; Article_13 §3.1 Principles]

feature.name: Virtual_Model
feature.description: In OpenFlexo, a container for FlexoConcepts that federates information from multiple sources. Trace: [Article_13 §3.1 Principles; Article_13 §3.2 How models federation takes place?]

feature.name: FlexoConcept
feature.description: A conceptual entity in OpenFlexo representing an n-ary relationship between ModellingElements from different models, carrying contextual semantics. Trace: [Article_13 §3.1 Principles]

feature.name: ConceptRole
feature.description: Assigns a name to a ModellingElement reference within a FlexoConcept definition. Trace: [Article_13 §3.1 Principles]

feature.name: Links
feature.description: Relationships and dependencies that connect models and their elements within the federation.

feature.name: Dependency
feature.description: A relationship where one model depends on the output attributes of another, forming edges in the multi-model graph. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Change Propagation]

feature.name: Inter_Viewpoint_Relationship
feature.description: A link between elements of different viewpoint models in a multimodel, with specific semantics like implication or impact. Trace: [Article_12 §III.E Definition of inter-viewpoint relationships]

feature.name: Implication
feature.description: An element in one viewpoint implies an element in another viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12 §III.E Definition of inter-viewpoint relationships]

feature.name: Exclusion
feature.description: An element in one viewpoint excludes an element in another viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12 §III.E Definition of inter-viewpoint relationships]

feature.name: Impact
feature.description: An element in one viewpoint impacts a quality attribute or element in another viewpoint. Trace: [Article_12 §III.E Definition of inter-viewpoint relationships]

feature.name: Security_Rule
feature.description: A rule attached to a link in a security-oriented federation to check consistency upon model evolution. Trace: [Article_11 §III.A.2 Build the security model federation]

feature.name: Formalism
feature.description: The modeling languages and paradigms used for the constituent models.

feature.name: Domain_Specific_Modeling_Language
feature.description: A modeling language tailored to a specific domain, allowing precise abstraction of domain constructs. Trace: [Article_1 §Abstract; Article_13 §2.1 Domain Specific Modeling]

feature.name: General_Purpose_Modeling_Language
feature.description: A modeling language like UML or SysML used across domains, often extended with profiles. Trace: [Article_1 §1 Introduction; Article_11 §II.A Security by design]

feature.name: Formalism_Extension
feature.description: Extensions to standard languages to incorporate additional concerns, such as security annotations. Trace: [Article_11 §II.A Security by design]

feature.name: UMLsec
feature.description: A UML profile for security, adding stereotypes and constraints. Trace: [Article_11 §II.A Security by design]

feature.name: SecBPMN
feature.description: A BPMN extension with security annotations. Trace: [Article_11 §II.A Security by design]

feature.name: Domain
feature.description: The application domain or system context in which the model federation is applied.

feature.name: Automotive
feature.description: Automotive software product lines as an example domain. Trace: [Article_12 §III.A Establishing the goal of the multimodel]

feature.name: Radar_Systems
feature.description: Radar system design involving signal processing and architecture models. Trace: [Article_13 §2.2 Model Based System Engineering]

feature.name: Medical_Application
feature.description: Healthcare systems like iTrust, focusing on security requirements. Trace: [Article_11 §IV Case Study]

feature.name: Traffic_Light_Control
feature.description: A traffic light control system used as an experimental multi-model. Trace: [Article_1 §5 Experiments]

feature.name: Technological_Context
feature.description: The tools, platforms, and technical infrastructure supporting the federation.

feature.name: Connectors
feature.description: Software components that connect individual models to the multi-model, enabling controlled information exchange. Trace: [Article_1 §3.3 Connectors]

feature.name: Technology_Adapter
feature.description: In OpenFlexo, a connector handling a specific technology and providing ModelSlots for accessing resources. Trace: [Article_13 §3.1 Principles]

feature.name: ModelSlot
feature.description: In OpenFlexo, a symbolic link to a resource in the Information Space, exposing its structure and behavior to the Concept Space. Trace: [Article_13 §3.1 Principles]

feature.name: Repository
feature.description: A version-controlled storage for all federation artifacts, enabling reconstruction and collaboration. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 NAOMI Multi-model Repository]

feature.name: Sandbox
feature.description: A local copy of the repository allowing modelers to work independently and synchronize changes. Trace: [Article_1 §3.1 Sandboxes]

feature.name: Version_Control_System
feature.description: A system like Subversion that manages artifact versions and enables rollback and synchronization. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Version Management]

feature.name: Execution_Engine
feature.description: A component that determines an order of execution based on dependencies and orchestrates model execution. Trace: [Article_1 §3.3 Execution Automation Engine]

feature.name: Multi_Model_Manager
feature.description: A component assisting modelers in integrating connectors, performing consistency checks, and visualizing the repository. Trace: [Article_1 §3.3 Multi-Model Manager]

feature.name: Operational
feature.description: Includes the processes, operations, and triggers in Model Federation, focusing on querying, synchronization, validation, and management of federated models and links.

feature.name: Data_Exchange
feature.description: The mechanism for sharing data between models via attributes, where owners write attributes and readers synchronize to access them. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Data Exchange]

feature.name: Model_Execution
feature.description: The process of reading input attributes, running the model using its DSML tool, and writing output attributes. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Model Execution]

feature.name: Change_Propagation
feature.description: The coordinated propagation of changes from one model to dependent models based on dependency analysis. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Change Propagation]

feature.name: Dependency_Graph_Analysis
feature.description: Analyzing the graph of model dependencies to determine an order for change propagation. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Change Propagation]

feature.name: Execution_Rules
feature.description: User-defined rules specifying system behavior for nondeterministic models or cyclic dependencies. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Change Propagation]

feature.name: Consistency_Management
feature.description: Ensuring that the multi-model remains consistent after changes, covering various consistency types.

feature.name: Attribute_Consistency
feature.description: All attributes have been updated by their owner model since the last change to their owner's input attributes. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Consistency Management]

feature.name: Constraint_Consistency
feature.description: The current values of all attributes do not violate any model-specific constraints. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Consistency Management]

feature.name: Attribute_Model_Consistency
feature.description: The modification times of all models are earlier than the modification times of their output attributes. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Consistency Management]

feature.name: NAOMI_Consistency
feature.description: A multi-model that is attribute consistent, constraint consistent, and attribute-model consistent. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Consistency Management]

feature.name: Synchronization
feature.description: The process of keeping federated models aligned, either automatically or interactively, across technological spaces. Trace: [Article_13 §4.1 Model synchronization]

feature.name: Validation
feature.description: Checking constraints and security rules attached to links to detect inconsistencies. Trace: [Article_11 §III.B Using the security model federation]

feature.name: Querying
feature.description: Querying the federated models to extract cross-cutting views or information. Trace: [Article_13 §2.4 Synthesis]

feature.name: Version_Management
feature.description: Managing multiple versions of models and tools, supporting rollback and reconstruction. Trace: [Article_1 §3.2 Version Management]

feature.name: Intentional
feature.description: Addresses the objectives and goals of Model Federation, such as traceability, consistency assurance, transformation management, composition, and conceptual elicitation.

feature.name: Traceability
feature.description: Maintaining traceability links between artifacts across domains and technological spaces for horizontal and vertical traceability. Trace: [Article_13 §2.4 Synthesis]

feature.name: Consistency_Assurance
feature.description: Ensuring global consistency across heterogeneous models and viewpoints. Trace: [Article_1 §2.2 Challenge 2: Maintaining Multi-model Consistency; Article_13 §1 Introduction]

feature.name: Transformation_Management
feature.description: Managing model-to-model transformations and data transformations during inter-model exchange. Trace: [Article_1 §2.4 Requirements; Article_13 §4.2 Model mapping]

feature.name: Composition
feature.description: Composing multiple models into a coherent multi-model or system representation. Trace: [Article_1 §Abstract; Article_12 §Abstract]

feature.name: Conceptual_Elicitation
feature.description: Deriving new concepts and relationships from federated models to support reasoning and analysis. Trace: [Article_13 §3.1 Principles]

feature.name: Security_By_Design
feature.description: Integrating security requirements from early design phases and ensuring consistent evolution of secured models. Trace: [Article_11 §II.A Security by design]

feature.name: Interoperability
feature.description: Achieving interoperability between heterogeneous models, tools, and formalisms.

feature.name: Technical_Interoperability
feature.description: Physical connectivity and data exchange between simulation systems. Trace: [Article_10 §III.A Technical Interoperability]

feature.name: Substantive_Interoperability
feature.description: Meaningful data exchange and coherent interaction based on shared conceptual frameworks. Trace: [Article_10 §III.B Substantive Interoperability]

feature.name: Conceptual_Interoperability
feature.description: Reconciling heterogeneous viewpoints through model federation to enable consistent reasoning. Trace: [Article_13 §Abstract]

feature.name: Reusability
feature.description: Enabling reuse of models and components across different simulation scenarios. Trace: [Article_10 §II.A Reusability and Interoperability]

feature.name: Composability
feature.description: The capability to select and assemble simulation components into valid systems to satisfy requirements. Trace: [Article_10 §II.B Composability and Interoperability]
